views: Migrate ColorTrackingVectorImageButton icons to ui::ColorId

This CL simplifies `ColorTrackingVectorImageButton` by passing its icon
`ui::ColorId`s directly to `SetImageFromVectorIconWithColor()`.
Previously, `OnThemeChanged()` resolved the normal and disabled icon
colors through `GetColorProvider()` and passed the resulting SkColors.

Following crrev.com/c/7089438, `views::IconColors` takes
`ui::ColorVariant`s. The icon images and the ink drop base color now
resolve the color ids against the current color provider when they are
painted or created, so they automatically handle theme changes.

Revert CHECK to DCHECK in EnterFullscreenModeForTab()

FullscreenController::CanEnterFullscreenModeForTab() can return false
when EnterFullscreenModeForTab() is called on Android, causing a
non-fatal CHECK dump in release builds. Revert the CHECK back to DCHECK
with a CHECK-exclusion comment while crbug.com/576177579 is
investigated.

Don't send Connection-Allowlist reports for history navigations

NavigationRequest::IsAllowedByConnectionAllowlist() checks the
navigation URL against the initiator's Connection-Allowlist policies and
queues a violation report containing that URL to the initiator's
reporting endpoint. For session history navigations, the URL comes from
the session history entry instead of the initiator, so any page could
use history.go(-n) with a report-only policy to learn the full URLs of
other pages in the tab's session history.

The check also ran from the speculative preconnect path in the
NavigationRequest constructor, so reports were queued even for history
navigations that are rejected later (e.g. from a sandboxed iframe
without allow-top-navigation).

Stop queueing reports for history navigations and for the preconnect
check. History navigations are still subject to the enforced policy.

Similarly, LoadingPredictorTabHelper tags its speculative requests
(preconnects, preresolves, LCPP prefetches) for a navigation with the
initiator's network restrictions ID, so the network service would check
them against the initiator's Connection-Allowlist and report violations
containing the history entry's origin and its predicted subresources.
Skip the LoadingPredictor's work for history navigations whose
initiator has a Connection-Allowlist.

Based on a CodeMender-generated patch.

x11: Reject incomplete UTF-16 selection payloads

RefCountedMemoryToString16 rounds the incoming byte count down when sizing
its UTF-16 destination, then asks span::copy_from to copy the entire source.
An odd-length selection therefore fails the equal-size CHECK. This can be
reached while parsing external text/x-moz-url drag data; a synthetic 67-byte
payload reproduces SIGTRAP in the existing conversion.

Reject incomplete UTF-16 code units before allocation and copying. Complete
code units and empty input retain their existing behavior. Add regression
tests for odd byte counts, empty input, and preservation of embedded NULs,
non-ASCII text, and surrogate pairs.

Related report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52249

Validation: A focused harness using the unchanged production function and
Chromium's span/CHECK headers reproduces SIGTRAP before the change and passes
all 4098 tested byte lengths (0..4097) afterward under ASan and UBSan. The
harness substitutes STL-backed ref-counted storage and supplies generated
build flags locally. Formatting and git diff --check pass.

Chromium's upload presubmit reports no errors. Its one warning notes that
the sparse checkout has not been initialized with gclient sync.

The Chromium ozone_x11_unittests target and end-to-end application drag/drop
have not been run. The guard prevents the malformed payload from crashing
the process; it does not repair a sender's incorrectly encoded drag data.

FSA: Fail showDirectoryPicker() if the mount point was revoked

On ChromeOS, a directory on an external mount point (e.g. a removable
volume) is picked as a virtual path, and DidChooseDirectory() cracks it
into a FileSystemURL only after the permission prompt is accepted. If
the mount point is revoked while the prompt is showing, the URL is
invalid, but a directory handle was still created for it. Passing that
handle to isSameEntry() of a file handle reaches NOTREACHED() in
SerializeURLImpl().

Reject with NotFoundError instead, the same as GetChildURL() does for
children of a directory whose mount point has been revoked.

2c8c57a060fd2222f414842db9874b9a7cd91b9e [ diff ] 
[actor] Do not destroy OffscreenRenderingManager if WebContents active

When stopping offscreen rendering for a Tab, OffscreenRenderingManager
currently checks if (mOffscreenTabs.isEmpty()) { destroy(); } without
checking whether standalone WebContents (such as the Glic web client)
are still actively rendering offscreen.

When the last offscreen Tab stops while a standalone WebContents remains
active, destroy() is erroneously invoked. This forcibly stops and
detaches the WebContents, sets its top-level native window to null,
destroys the native compositor, and clears the singleton manager. As a
result, the remaining WebContents stops receiving BeginFrames and is
left in a detached state.

This CL updates stopOffscreenRendering(Tab) to check both
mOffscreenTabs.isEmpty() && mOffscreenWebContents.isEmpty() before
destroying the manager, matching the condition used in
stopOffscreenRendering(WebContents).

[svg] Use the replaced content rect for embedded SVG documents

When the flag SVGEmbeddedAsReplacedElement is enabled, object-fit and
object-position apply to in-process SVG documents in <object> and
<embed>. The child frame is sized and positioned by the replaced content
rect, but coordinate mapping still uses the offset of the content box.
When the replaced content rect has a different offset, pointer events
get the wrong target and coordinates, scrollIntoView scrolls to the
wrong position, and IntersectionObserver reports wrong results.

LocalFrameView and LayoutView now map between the child and parent
documents using the offset of the replaced content rect.

Since object-fit can also extend the child frame beyond the content box,
visual rects mapped out of the child document are clipped by the
LayoutEmbeddedObject. Where the child frame covers only part of the
content box, pointer events over the rest now target the <object> or
<embed> element instead of the child frame.

Changes to object-fit or object-position only invalidate paint, so the
child frame keeps its old size and position. With the flag enabled,
these changes on a LayoutEmbeddedObject now schedule a geometry update
in the parent LocalFrameView and a paint property update on the child
LayoutView.

Apart from the handling of style changes, these changes do not depend on
the flag. For other frames and plugins, the replaced content rect has
the same offset as the content box, so the offset used for coordinate
mapping does not change. The exception is a frame owner that is the
effective root scroller, whose replaced content rect has a zero offset.
Coordinate mapping now uses that offset, as painting and hit testing
already do.

Tests:
  /wpt/css/css-images/object-fit-change-svg-001o.html
  /wpt/css/css-images/object-fit-svg-intersection-observer.sub.html
  /wpt/css/css-images/object-fit-svg-pointer-events.html
  /wpt/css/css-images/object-fit-svg-scroll-into-view.html

[Actor] Only mark the most recent task notification as Live

Currently, with several actor tasks running, every task notification is
a promoted Live Update, so SystemUI picks the status chip among them on
its own and it often shows the wrong task.

Only the task whose notification category changed most recently is now
posted as live. When the live task changes, the previous one is
reposted as non-live, or demoted right away if it was a finished task
awaiting demotion. When the live task is demoted or removed, the next
most recent task becomes live.

Add per-tab session lifecycle tracking to CdpActorSessionTracker

Extend CdpActorSessionTracker with per-tab session lifecycle tracking:
- OnClientAttached(): tracks eligible tab-bound DevTools channels and
  immediately records built-in DevTools UI (kDevToolsUi) on
  TabCdpActorTracker.
- OnCommandHandled(): records external Pipe (kExternalPipe) and
  WebSocket (kExternalWebSocket) sessions on TabCdpActorTracker upon
  their first CDP command dispatch, ignoring passive attachments.
- OnClientDetached(): detaches recorded actors from TabCdpActorTracker.
- GetEventInitiatorInfo(): returns per-tab EventInitiatorInfo for
  eligible BrowserContexts.

62111ea912ca40afc465238d8d6db471a43a80d7 [ diff ] 
Content: Use JniUniquePtr in TracingController

TracingControllerAndroidImpl stores its native
::content::TracingControllerAndroid address in a raw Java long field.
Passing untyped integer handles across the JNI boundary bypasses
compile-time type checking and ownership enforcement, exposing callers
to use-after-free bugs if the peer is used after teardown.

Declare a package-private NativeTracingControllerAndroid JniTypeToken
mapped to ::content::TracingControllerAndroid and hold the Java-owned
peer in a JniUniquePtr<NativeTracingControllerAndroid> allocated via
jni_zero::MakeUnique. Pass the handle to @NativeMethods calls using
JniPtr<NativeTracingControllerAndroid> and destroy the native peer via
destroy().

ash: Remove redundant PrinterErrorCode enum asserts

`printer_error_codes.cc` asserts that `chromeos::PrinterErrorCode` and
the print_management mojom enum have the same values. Nothing casts
between the two: `PrinterErrorCodeToMojom()` converts with an exhaustive
switch. Remove the asserts and the mojom dependency. Also drop an unused
include.

[ui] Delegate TabStripModel::IsTabClosable() to UnloadController

Forced browser close paths (such as chrome::ExitIgnoreUnloadHandlers()
and Browser::~Browser()) call
UnloadController::set_force_skip_warning_user_on_close(true) before
UnloadController::OnWindowClosing() invokes
TabStripModel::CloseAllTabs().

Previously, TabStripModel::IsTabClosable() queried
WebAppPolicyManager::IsPreventCloseEnabled() directly without checking
UnloadController::force_skip_warning_user_on_close(). For web app
windows with PreventClose enabled, CloseAllTabs() skipped closing the
app tab and left it in TabStripModel into ~Browser().

BrowserWindowFeatures::TearDownPreBrowserWindowDestruction() then
destroyed ExclusiveAccessManager before window_.reset() ran
BrowserView::OnWidgetDestroying() - which detached the remaining tab
and caused Browser::OnTabClosing() to dereference the destroyed
ExclusiveAccessManager.

Delegate TabStripModel::IsTabClosable() through TabStripModelDelegate
to UnloadController::IsTabClosable() - matching
ShouldRunUnloadListenerBeforeClosing() and
RunUnloadListenerBeforeClosing().

Return true from UnloadController::IsTabClosable() when
force_skip_warning_user_on_close_ is true so forced window closes
empty TabStripModel before Browser teardown.

[Files] Flatten `excludedUrls` in `XfDlpRestrictionDetailsDialog`

In `XfDlpRestrictionDetailsDialog`, `excludedUrls` was populated via
`excludedUrls.push(exceptDetails.urls)`. Because `exceptDetails.urls` is
an array of strings, `excludedUrls` became an array of string arrays.
When formatting via `excludedUrls.join(', ')`, each nested array was
coerced to a string with `toString()`, joining multiple URLs under the
same level with raw commas rather than proper separators.

This CL explicitly types `excludedUrls` as `string[]` and flattens
elements using the spread operator. A unit test is also added to
`xf_dlp_restriction_details_dialog_unittest.ts` to verify formatting
when multiple URLs are excluded from a wildcard.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[net] Re-enable `URLRequestQuicWithTcpTest` cases on Android Debug

`AltServiceRightCert`,
`AltServiceWrongCertSimultaneousNonAltServiceQuicAttempt`,
`AltServiceWrongCertSimultaneousNonAltServiceQuicAttemptReverseOrder`,
`AltServiceWrongCertExistingNonAltServiceQuicSession`,
`TwoAltServiceRequestsOneWrongCert`,
`TwoAltServiceRequestsOneWrongCertReverseOrder`, and
`AltServiceRequestWrongCertExistingAltServiceQuicSession` in
`net/url_request/url_request_quic_unittest.cc` were disabled on Android
Debug builds in https://crrev.com/c/7766879
(https://crbug.com/503402050).

At that time, `CreateQuicSimpleServerSocket` unconditionally enabled
`SO_REUSEADDR` (`socket->AllowAddressReuse()`) even when binding to
ephemeral port `0`, and `URLRequestQuicTest::StartQuicServer` listened
on `IPAddress::IPv4AllZeros()` (`0.0.0.0:0`) instead of
`IPAddress::IPv4Localhost()` (`127.0.0.1:0`), allowing duplicate
ephemeral port bindings across parallel test processes and routing
shadowing. Additionally, `URLRequestQuicTest` stored
`base::test::ScopedFeatureList` as a subclass member destroyed before
`TestWithTaskEnvironment`'s `TaskEnvironment`. Subsequently,
https://crrev.com/c/8260428 migrated `URLRequestQuicTest` to
`AddScopedFeatureList()`, and https://crrev.com/c/8266656 removed
`AllowAddressReuse()` on ephemeral port `0` in
`CreateQuicSimpleServerSocket` and changed
`URLRequestQuicTest::StartQuicServer` to bind to
`IPAddress::IPv4Localhost()`.

Re-enable all seven `URLRequestQuicWithTcpTest` cases on Android Debug

[Net] Re-enable `UDPSocketTest.LocalBroadcast` on Android

`UDPSocketTest.LocalBroadcast` (originally `UDPSocketTest.Broadcast`)
was disabled on Android in https://crrev.com/168010 because Android
devices attached to test bots lacked a default network interface, so
broadcasting to `255.255.255.255` failed with `ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE`
(`-109`).

Subsequently, https://crrev.com/c/1262596 updated the test to broadcast
to the loopback subnet broadcast address `127.255.255.255` instead of
`255.255.255.255`, which routes over the loopback interface without
requiring an external default network. In addition,
https://crrev.com/c/1385017 replaced the hardcoded UDP port `9999` with
an OS-assigned ephemeral port via `UDPServerSocket::GetLocalAddress()`.

This CL re-enables `UDPSocketTest.LocalBroadcast` on Android and adds
documentation comments for the test.

Verified on Android 15 phone and Android 15 tablet emulators.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

1c3ffcfd250209f438c8ec9a6e8d929d9fe87118 [ diff ] 
proto_extras: remove //base dependency from protoc plugins

Currently, //components/proto_extras:proto_extras_plugin and
:proto_test_extras_plugin depend on //base for a few string/path
utilities (base::FilePath::ReplaceExtension, base::StrCat,
base::ToUpperASCII, base::ReplaceChars, base::flat_set, and CHECK).

In component builds, linking against //base forces proto_extras_plugin
to wait for libbase.so (and its 10-step Rust dependency chain, finishing
at ~76s on 128-core bots) before any of the 28 proto_extras codegen
actions can run. Because proto_extras targets use a source_set wrapper
around action_foreach, GN propagates hard_deps across all transitive
dependents, blocking >5,600 downstream C++ compile steps in
//components, //content/browser, and //chrome/browser until ~80s into
the build.

Replace the //base utilities in proto_extras_plugin.cc and
proto_test_extras_plugin.cc with standard C++ (<algorithm>, <cstdlib>,
<iostream>, <set>, <string>), Abseil (absl::AsciiStrToUpper,
ABSL_UNREACHABLE), and google::protobuf::compiler::cpp::StripProto, and
add assert_no_deps = [ "//base" ] and a -base DEPS rule to both plugin
targets to prevent regressing this dependency in the future. This allows
proto_extras_plugin to link alongside protoc (~22s) without waiting for
libbase.so (~76s), unblocking all proto_extras actions ~54s earlier.

[ARC] Use USER_VISIBLE priority in ArcWallpaperService::GetWallpaper

During ARC boot, Android SystemUIService (ThemeOverlayController)
synchronously blocks on the GetWallpaper() Mojo call before starting
StatusBar and KeyguardService.

Previously, ArcWallpaperService::GetWallpaper() posted PNG encoding to
base::ThreadPool with BEST_EFFORT priority. When Chrome logs in without
a browser window, AfterStartupTaskUtils holds the best-effort execution
fence until its timeout expires, starving GetWallpaper() and stalling
Android SystemUI and KeyguardService initialization.

Use USER_VISIBLE priority so GetWallpaper() is not blocked by the
startup best-effort execution fence.

Use a common Flags function for StyleRecalcChange child traversal

We traverse children during style recalc based on:

- ChildNeedsStyleRecalc()
- The Propagate enum for inheritance and forced descendant recalc
- Flags for invalidating style for container query dependent, and for
  content-visibility inside elements with a scroll-marker-group

Another flag will be added to invalidate precomputed :hover styles,
which means another condition will be added to
StylRecalcChange::TraverseChildren() and triggering the actual
RecalcOwnStyle().

Instead of adding a new condition, make a common RecalcFlagDependent()
function to simplify the code a bit.

[FSA] Re-enable `ConfirmSensitiveEntryAccess_BlockChildrenNested`

`ChromeFileSystemAccessPermissionContextTest` test
`ConfirmSensitiveEntryAccess_BlockChildrenNested` was disabled in
https://crrev.com/c/6733488 due to flakiness after
https://crrev.com/c/6692873 moved block-path normalization into an
asynchronous thread pool task started by
`ChromeFileSystemAccessPermissionContext` during `SetUp()`. That
unsequenced constructor task raced with the subsequent
`ResetBlockPath()` call after `ScopedPathOverride` was applied in the
test body, allowing stale non-overridden block rules to overwrite the
test's overridden rules.

The race was resolved in https://crrev.com/c/6815979 by removing the
constructor `ResetBlockPaths()` call and initializing block rules lazily
on the first blocklist check. Re-enable the test now that the racing
constructor task is gone. Verified on Linux.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

FSA: Reject symlinks in macOS copy-on-write swap file creation

On macOS, `FileSystemAccessFileHandleImpl::CreateClonedSwapFile()`
creates `.crswap` files for `createWritable({keepExistingData: true})`
by calling `clonefile(source, swap, /*flags=*/0)` in
`CreateCowSwapFile()`.

Because `LocalFileUtil::GetLocalFilePath()` hides symlinks by mapping
them to `FILE_ERROR_NOT_FOUND`, the preceding `FileExists(swap_url)`
probe reports a pre-existing symlink at `<name>.crswap` as
`FILE_ERROR_NOT_FOUND`. When `<name>.crswap` is a dangling symlink,
`clonefile()` with `flags=0` follows the destination symlink and creates
the cloned file at the symlink's target. Similarly, if the source path
was replaced with a symlink, `clonefile()` would follow it.

Check `base::IsLink()` on `source_url.path()` (returning
`FILE_ERROR_NOT_FOUND`) and `swap_url.path()` (returning
`FILE_ERROR_EXISTS` so `DidCloneSwapFile()` advances to the next unused
swap filename) before invoking `clonefile()`.

[ReadingList] Check URL support for Add Link to Reading List menu item

This CL updates the context menu `Add Link to Reading List` command to
verify that the `ReadingListModel` is loaded and supports the link URL
before showing, enabling, or executing the command.

Previously, `RenderViewContextMenu` unconditionally appended the menu
item for non-image links and only checked `link_url.is_valid()`,
allowing non-HTTP/HTTPS links such as `mailto:` or `javascript:` to be
added to the `ReadingListModel`. Because `ReadingListEntry` only
supports HTTP and HTTPS URLs, syncing such an entry triggered a crash
in `ClientTagBasedDataTypeProcessor::Put` when validating entity data.

[protobuf] Wire new-patch and fixup CLI and agent guide in README

`NewPatch`, `FixupPatch`, and fixup conflict recovery are implemented in
`roll_protobuf.py`, and the earlier milestones already expose `check`,
`plan`, `prepare`, `start`, `status`, `continue`, `drop`, `resume`,
`generate`, and `abort`.

Without CLI subcommands for `new-patch` and `fixup` or explicit
guardrails in `README.chromium`, human rollers and supervised AI coding
agents still lack CLI entry points for creating or amending patches and
clear rules on which actions require human approval.

Wire `new-patch <patch>` and `fixup <patch>` (plus dirty-worktree next
command ordering in `GetRollStatus`) into `roll_protobuf.py` CLI and
document `new-patch`, `fixup`, and "Using an agent:" in
`//third_party/protobuf/README.chromium`.

parent
b5764be4fa8841284f4c8008cfd45e02af9cffce [ diff ] 
[protobuf] Support fixup rebase conflicts in status, abort, and guards

While `FixupPatch` and `ContinueRoll` can start and resume a conflicting
`fixup` rebase, `GetRollStatus` and `AbortRoll` still only inspect
`state.json`, and other mutating subcommands (`prepare`, `drop`,
`resume`, `start`, and `generate`) do not check for an in-progress git
rebase or stale `fixup.json`.

Running `status` or `abort` during a paused `fixup` rebase therefore
fails to report or roll back `pre_fixup_head` while preserving
`state.json`, and running another roll subcommand mid-rebase can corrupt
working-tree state.

Extend `GetRollStatus`, `FormatRollStatusReport`, and `AbortRoll` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to report and abort active
`fixup` rebases (`fixup.json`), restoring `pre_fixup_head` while
preserving any underlying `state.json`, and add active-rebase guards to
`PrepareRoll`, `DropCurrentPatch`, `ResumeRoll`, `StartRoll`, and
`GenerateBootstrapFiles`.

[protobuf] Add _ContinueFixupRebase for conflicting fixup rebases

When `roll_protobuf.py fixup` stops on a downstream rebase conflict, it
persists `fixup.json` and instructs the user to resolve the conflict and
run `roll_protobuf.py continue`, but `ContinueRoll` currently only
handles `state.json` `conflict` state from `start` or `resume`.

Without `_ContinueFixupRebase` wired into `ContinueRoll`, users cannot
resume a conflicting `fixup` rebase, step through multi-commit rebase
conflicts, or automatically rewrite `patches/*.patch` once the rebase
completes.

Add `_ContinueFixupRebase` and wire `ContinueRoll` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to validate conflict
resolution and scope hygiene across patch and non-patch rebase steps,
roll back to `pre_fixup_head` if a resolved patch becomes empty, and
finalize `patches/*.patch` when the rebase finishes.

[protobuf] Add unmerged-index and rebase-matching helpers for fixup

`_LoadActiveFixupState` currently checks only whether a git rebase
directory exists alongside `fixup.json`, and
`_FindFilesWithConflictMarkers` only detects textual `<<<<<<<` conflict
markers in working-tree files.

If a user aborts the `fixup` rebase and starts an unrelated `git rebase`
(or hits a modify/delete or binary conflict that leaves unmerged index
stages without textual conflict markers), `roll_protobuf.py` could
misidentify the active rebase or allow `continue` to stage unresolved
files.

Add `_IsMatchingFixupRebase`, `_CommitTouchedPaths`, and
`_FindUnresolvedUnmergedPaths` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to verify `onto` and
`orig-head~1` against `FixupState`, sync live `(index, total)` rebase
counters, and compare working-tree blob OIDs against index stages 2 and
3 to catch markerless unmerged files.

[protobuf] Add FixupPatch for roll_protobuf.py fixup

Amending an earlier `"Apply patches/NNNN-*.patch"` commit on a roll
branch currently requires manually creating a `fixup!` commit, running
`git rebase -i --autosquash`, and regenerating every downstream
`patches/*.patch` file whose line numbers or context shifted.

Performing that rebase by hand risks leaving `patches/*.patch` files or
`state.json` `expected_head` out of sync with the rewritten commits, or
leaving an untracked git rebase state if a downstream patch conflicts.

Add `FixupResult`, `_FinalizeCompletedFixup`, `FixupPatch`, and
`FormatFixupReport` in `//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to fold
uncommitted `src/` and `python/` edits into an earlier patch commit via
non-interactive `git rebase --interactive --autosquash`, rewrite
`patches/*.patch` along the branch, and persist `fixup.json` with
recovery instructions when a rebase conflict occurs.

[protobuf] Add FixupState and target-patch lookup for fixup

`roll_protobuf.py` currently persists roll progress in `state.json`
(`GITDIR/protobuf-roll/state.json`), but has no state model for tracking
an in-progress `fixup` interactive rebase or resolving a user-supplied
patch identifier to its `"Apply patches/NNNN-*.patch"` commit on the
current branch.

Without persistent `fixup.json` metadata and target-commit lookup
helpers, `roll_protobuf.py fixup` cannot validate that a target patch is
applied once and not dropped later on the branch, or recover cleanly
when `git rebase --interactive --autosquash` stops on a conflict.

Add `FixupState`, `_SaveFixupState`, `_RemoveFixupState`,
`LoadFixupState`, `_LoadActiveFixupState`, `_IsGitRebaseInProgress`,
`_RebaseGitEnvironment`, `_ResolveFixupRebaseBase`,
`_FindTargetPatchCommit`, and `_BuildFixupConflictState` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` with unit tests in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf_test.py`.

[protobuf] Add _RewritePatchFilesAlongBranch for roll_protobuf.py fixup

When an earlier `Apply patches/NNNN-*.patch` commit on a roll branch is
amended via `git rebase --autosquash`, downstream patch files whose line
numbers or context shifted become stale, and any rebased manual
`"Regenerate bootstrap files"` commit loses its link to the pre-rebase
generator inputs.

Leaving shifted `.patch` files unrefreshed causes `roll_protobuf.py
check` or the next upstream roll to fail, and losing the pre-rebase
generator digest hides stale bootstrap files when an amended patch
touches compiler sources.

Add `_RewritePatchFilesAlongBranch` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` to rebuild `patches/*.patch`
blobs in commit order via `_UpdatePatchesSubtree` without checking out
intermediate commits, stamp pre-rebase `Bootstrap-Inputs-Hash` trailers
onto manual regeneration commits when generator inputs change, and sync
the refreshed `.patch` files to disk and `.git/index`.

[protobuf] Add git tree and bootstrap-digest helpers for fixup

`roll_protobuf.py` currently computes bootstrap generator input digests
from the live working tree (`_ComputeBootstrapInputsDigest`) and has no
helpers for reading or updating `third_party/protobuf/patches/` subtrees
directly in the git object database.

To rewrite `patches/*.patch` files across a branch after a `fixup`
rebase without checking out intermediate commits or losing the link
between an amended generator patch and a downstream `"Regenerate
bootstrap files"` commit, `fixup` needs in-memory git tree manipulation
and commit-tree bootstrap digest helpers.

Add `_APPLY_PATCH_SUBJECT_PATTERN`, `_DROP_PATCH_SUBJECT_PATTERN`,
`_ListGitTree`, `_ReadPatchesSubtreeBlobs`, `_UpdatePatchesSubtree`,
`_ComputeCommitBootstrapDigest`, `_FindUnstampedRegenTarget`, and
`_PatchFileTouchesGenerator` in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf.py` with unit tests in
`//third_party/protobuf/roll_protobuf_test.py`.

bacf0cd455a4bb88c9b91ef5f0c4104813976f25 [ diff ] 
Forward text selection to SystemUI via ActionMode API

When the Android 26Q4 forward_text_selection_to_systemui flag is
enabled, SystemUI performs text classification in the remote floating
toolbar session using the selection context provided via
ActionMode.setTextSelection().

Update Chromium selection handling to use the new API when enabled:

- Add isForwardTextSelectionToSystemUiEnabled(), setTextSelection(),
  and clearTextSelection() methods to AconfigFlaggedApiDelegate.
- Skip redundant local TextClassifier.classifyText() calls in
  SmartSelectionProvider when the flag is enabled, no custom
  TextClassifier is set, and the selection menu uses ActionMode.
  Selection suggestion requests still run locally with
  setIncludeTextClassification(false).
- Forward the surrounding text, selection indices, and default locales
  to ActionMode.setTextSelection() in
  SelectionPopupControllerImpl.onPrepareActionMode() for non-password,
  non-incognito selections, and call ActionMode.clearTextSelection() in
  onDestroyActionMode().

[tvOS] Filter out DestroySurfaceEmbedChildAfterEmbedderProcessDied

The test kills the embedder's renderer with content::CrashTab(), but
tvOS runs in single-process mode, where RenderProcessHost::Shutdown()
returns false without doing anything. The renderer stays alive, so the
crash expectations in CrashTab() and the embedder frame node check that
follows it all fail.

1d3439ea5035e6e95a54218cfbf3dd7f14b6a50d [ diff ] 
[CAA] Show last uploaded signals report in connectors-internals

The signals JSON on chrome://connectors-internals/#signals-reporting
is generated on demand when the page is opened, without a challenge
from DMServer. Client certificates are only collected when a challenge
is available (each certificate signal signs it), so the page always
showed "certificates_count": 0 even when the reports actually uploaded
by ReportScheduler contained certificates. This made the page
misleading when debugging certificate collection. I also refactored the
last security report config field.

Tested-locally: https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/image/0doc3plfruktg.png

31a875e8aa6310fc4ffcbdf130c33336eb49530c [ diff ] 
Mark Performance.getEntries* with Affects=Nothing

- Context: DevTools Console eager evaluation and the DevTools AI
  executeJavaScript tool evaluate expressions with throwOnSideEffect:
  true. Because performance.getEntries(), getEntriesByType(), and
  getEntriesByName() lacked [Affects=Nothing], calling them aborted with
  EvalError: Possible side-effect in debug-evaluate.
- Why this was missed: Blink IDL attributes default to
  kHasNoSideEffect, whereas IDL methods default to kHasSideEffect unless
  explicitly annotated with [Affects=Nothing]. These three methods only
  read buffered PerformanceEntry records without mutating state.
- Prior art: performance.now() in the same interface is already marked
  [Affects=Nothing], and performance.timeOrigin, performance.timing, and
  performance.navigation are side-effect-free readonly attributes.

[Scroll Timing] Make shared buffer payload access lock-free

Replace the 32-byte atomic_ref<ScrollTimingInfo> with per-field
SharedAtomic values, which enforce lock-free access at compile time.
This avoids process-local locking fallbacks while preserving the
existing seqlock ordering and overwrite detection.

Remove the explicit padding and whole-record shared-memory assertions,
which are no longer needed for field-by-field copies. Destructure the
record in Push() so adding fields requires updating the transport.

Follow-up to the atomic_ref review comments in crrev.com/c/8478674.

[GPU] Re-enable `PointCoordTest.RenderTo` on Linux and ChromeOS

`PointCoordTest.RenderTo` was disabled in release builds on Linux (and
later ChromeOS via https://crrev.com/c/2351281) due to flakiness on an
old Linux ATI bot (https://crbug.com/40299409).

Git history was investigated and the exact repairing commit could not be
pinpointed, though `gl_tests` now runs on ANGLE/SwANGLE and modern Mesa
drivers. Re-enable `PointCoordTest.RenderTo`. Verified on Linux.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Cronet] Add HTTP flag to disable setIdempotency calls

Introduce the Cronet_disable_set_idempotency HTTP flag. When enabled,
calls to ExperimentalUrlRequest.Builder#setIdempotency are silently
ignored so that the request retains DEFAULT_IDEMPOTENCY.

[Cronet] Add HTTP flag to disable shared Brotli dictionaries

Introduce the Cronet_disable_shared_brotli HTTP flag. When enabled,
calls to UrlRequest.Builder#setRawCompressionDictionary are silently
ignored as a no-op (including skipping argument validation) so that
compression dictionaries are not attached to requests.

Use base::EnumSet and base::span for CryptAuth feature types

Replaces base::flat_set with base::EnumSet (as CryptAuthFeatureTypeSet)
for CryptAuth feature types, allowing the sets to be constructed and
passed efficiently by value without requiring heap allocation or
base::NoDestructor.

Also updates GetAllCryptAuthFeatureTypeStrings() to return a
base::span<const std::string_view> instead of a base::flat_set, and
updates call sites and unit tests to match.
